title: Choose the look of The Ranger's Road
question: Which direction should guide Keep, readiness, and the next Chapter I screens? Each keeps the documented program, safety rules, and color family.

options.label: Forest Light
options.lineage: trail dawn and naturalist field notes
options.thesis: A calm daily mission board with one spare forest scene to set the chapter's place.
options.viewport: A narrow forest dawn sits behind Chapter I; campaign day, Today's Orders, readiness, and Begin Today's Mission stay readable on the first phone screen.
options.risk: Scenery could steal space from the day's orders if the image grows too large.

raised.raise: The readiness message changes in plain words while its visual surroundings remain steady.
Full and reduced missions keep the same structure, making the adjustment easy to compare.
A strict text rhythm keeps dates, labels, and actions legible even over an atmospheric surface.
The day's watch and main order read as a repeatable sequence with one clear current step.
Primary mission text gets poster-like scan speed without turning every task into a tile.

options.label: Field Ledger
options.thesis: The campaign reads like a well-kept field record with clean rules and margin cues.
options.viewport: Chapter I occupies a compact masthead; campaign counts and Today's Orders sit in a ruled ledger, with readiness and the mission action clearly separated.
options.risk: It is the familiar ranger-journal choice and could feel too much like a form if the typography lacks warmth.

options.label: Night Atlas
options.lineage: a chart used for navigation after dark
options.thesis: The campaign becomes a quiet chart, with today marked as a clear point along the route.
options.viewport: A compact plotted Chapter I route frames day 1 and the Gate Trial; the current mission appears as a readable chart entry below it.
options.case: Outdoor navigation resonates with the audience; a chart asks more interpretation than a daily mission list.
options.risk: Coordinates and chart marks may obscure the task if they become more detailed than the orders.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.thesis: Words would reshape the scene around each mission state.
options.viewport: Mission words gather into a weather scene before settling into readable orders.
options.case: The interaction demands attention that a quick readiness check cannot spare.
options.risk: Animated type would slow the first task of the day.
options.kept: Readiness changes receive immediate, explicit text feedback.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.lineage: a garment shaped by one functional pull
options.thesis: One control would gather a full mission into a reduced version.
options.viewport: Readiness appears as a shaped mission plan with a visible full-to-reduced transition.
options.case: The adaptation idea is useful, but the garment metaphor does not clarify daily work.
options.risk: A bespoke control could hide a safety decision behind a gesture.
options.kept: Full and reduced missions retain the same information order.

options.label: Typewriter Scene
options.lineage: a picture built from character density
options.thesis: A text grid would draw the landscape and hold the mission details.
options.viewport: A character-grid forest surrounds a compact daily status and task list.
options.case: The strict grid aids rhythm, but its scenic texture makes small text harder to read.
options.risk: Character art would compete with instructional copy.
options.kept: Dates, status, and actions follow a disciplined text rhythm.

options.label: Rhythm Machine
options.lineage: a step sequencer with a moving position
options.thesis: Morning watch, main order, and evening watch would form a lit daily row.
options.viewport: A step row leads into today's mission details and current readiness.
options.case: The sequence is useful, but bright step controls feel like a game or instrument.
options.risk: Repeated illumination could turn ordinary practice into a streak mechanic.
options.kept: The day's work has a clear order and current step.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.lineage: large type on flat content tiles
options.thesis: Big words and flat blocks would make each mission scannable at a glance.
options.viewport: A bold Today's Orders tile fills the phone's first screen, with readiness and navigation in adjacent blocks.
options.case: The tile grid scans quickly but gives little room to the quiet field-journal character.
options.risk: Oversized tiles could push guidance and safety status below the fold.
options.kept: The main order gets immediate visual priority.

canonCard.label: Classic field journal
canonCard.thesis: The expected ranger-journal dashboard, carefully made and easy to use.
canonCard.viewport: A forest-green chapter card above simple Today's Orders, readiness, and the mission button, close to the current shell.
canonCard.risk: It stays familiar and may carry less of a distinct visual identity.
